own_solution.law: Bernoulli gives v = sqrt(2gh). Continuity gives A dh/dt = -a sqrt(2gh), hence t = (D/d)^2 sqrt(2/g)(sqrt(h0) - sqrt(h1)). Converting diameters to consistent units gives t = 323.2488 s. Widening the tank hole by q before timing multiplies this time by [10/(10+q)]^2, with q in mm.
assumptions: The open free surface and freely exiting jet are at atmospheric pressure.
Surface speed is negligible and jet area equals hole area throughout the interval.

notes: All certified answers agree with the draining equation: pre-timing tank-hole increases of 0.6, 1.3 and 1.9 mm give approximately 287.690, 253.151 and 228.267 s. Density cancels; the barrel and subsequent reaming have no causal path to the timed interval. The cancellation relations are consistent when p denotes hydrostatic gauge pressure. The explicitly claimed minimal pairs preserve the displayed number and unit. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal finding because pass 2 identifies T5A35 and T68EC as deliberate numeral-free controls, rather than claiming they preserve the numerical information of their twins. Their stated twin transformation accurately describes the text.
